intended_object: This is the natural bijection Hom(W, lim F) ≅ Cone(W, F) between morphisms from W into the limit of a diagram F and cones over F with cone point W, i.e. the universal property of the limit (the limit represents the cones functor). I inferred this from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
I judged this from the definition's body. I did not need to search further, because the counterpart is the very declaration it calls.

The definition takes the chosen limit of `F`, which exists because of `[HasLimit F]`, and applies the general `IsLimit.homIso` to it. That general isomorphism holds for any limit cone. It is an isomorphism in `Type` between `W ⟶ limit F` and `F.cones.obj (op W)`, the cones over `F` with cone point `W`. The `ULift` is only there to put both sides in the same universe, which is a harmless technicality.

The definition is stated for an arbitrary diagram `F : J ⥤ C` and any object `W`, so it already has its natural generality. It is the standard convenience specialization of `IsLimit.homIso` to the chosen limit `limit F`, and it matches the textbook statement that `lim F` represents the cones functor.
